featured_reviews.name: Roshani Batra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Chai Pe Charcha is one of those places that instantly feels cozy the moment you step in. It’s not just about chai here — it’s about conversations, comfort food, and even some fun with their collection of board games.

I tried two of their teas — the adrak chai and the kesar chai. The adrak chai had that strong, gingery warmth that wakes you up and feels like home. The kesar chai, on the other hand, was fragrant, creamy, and felt like a little indulgence in a cup. Both were perfectly brewed and served piping hot.

On the food side, the cheese Maggi was pure nostalgia — gooey, cheesy, and super comforting. But the star for me was the paneer bhurji with paratha. The paneer was soft and well-spiced, and the paratha paired beautifully with it — simple, hearty, and satisfying.

What I loved most though is the vibe of the place. It’s laid-back, student-friendly, and the board games make it a fun spot to spend time with friends while sipping chai. Prices are pocket-friendly too, which makes it even better.

If you’re a chai lover looking for a hangout spot that blends good food, great tea, and a chill atmosphere — this place should definitely be on your list!

We visited Nude Food Café as a group of five and, unfortunately, the experience didn’t go as well as we hoped. On the positive side, the café has a great eco-friendly concept with a zero-waste food policy, which I really appreciate. The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, even though the space feels a bit small and crowded.

The coffee was excellent, the chicken pie was tasty (could’ve used a spicy note), and the pasta dishes were nice, though one was slightly undercooked and could have used more spice. Portions felt a bit small for the price.

Overall, while the café’s concept and ambience are lovely, the extremely slow service and long wait time took away from the experience. Expanding the seating area or managing reservations more clearly would help a lot.

featured_reviews.name: Vishwesh Ranadive
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Trofima, Shivaji Park, Dadar, Mumbai

Cafe Trofima, located near the bustling Shivaji Park in Dadar, has garnered attention as a popular hangout spot, but it falls short of the hype for several reasons.

Food

The menu boasts a variety of food options, including breakfast platters, which might initially seem impressive. However, the taste of the food is compromised and does not justify the high prices. For a cafe that markets itself as a premium experience, the quality of the dishes leaves much to be desired.

Ambience and Seating

The sitting space is one of the better aspects of Cafe Trofima. Considering it is a cafe, the seating is comfortable and suitable for casual conversations or work. However, the overall ambience is just average, with no music to elevate the vibe. It lacks the warmth or charm that many would expect from a cafe in this area.

Service

The service is satisfactory but nothing extraordinary. While the staff is polite and attends to customers in a timely manner, the overall experience doesn’t stand out as memorable.

Location and Accessibility

A significant downside is the lack of parking space, which can be a hassle, especially given the busy location of Shivaji Park. Visitors arriving in their own vehicles may find it inconvenient.

Pricing

The prices are on the higher side, making it hard to justify for the quality of food and overall experience provided. While there are plenty of food options to choose from, the value for money is not reflected in the offerings.

Verdict

Cafe Trofima is overrated and doesn’t quite live up to its reputation. While it has some redeeming qualities like decent seating and satisfactory service, the compromised food taste, lack of parking, and high prices make it hard to recommend wholeheartedly. It could work as a one-time visit for those curious about its breakfast platters, but better options are available in and around the area for a more satisfying experience.

Overall Rating: 2/5

featured_reviews.name: Monica
featured_reviews.review_text:
If South Mumbai’s cafe culture had to be summed up in one place, this would be it. Cafe Free India brings together great food, a lively setting, and an atmosphere that keeps you hooked from the moment you walk in.

The space carries a strong Goan inspired vibe, paired with an energy that feels vibrant and effortless. What truly sets it apart is the 📍Live Karaoke hosted Four Times a week ( Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun, 9pm onwards ) It adds a sense of excitement to the entire experience and makes the place feel dynamic and interactive.

The food here leans towards indulgent comfort. The parmesan corn ribs are juicy and full of flavour, while the honey chilli lotus root stands out with the perfect balance of sweet and spice. Their pizzas are rich, cheesy, and consistently satisfying.

The drinks menu keeps things interesting with beers on tap and cocktails inspired by iconic parts of Mumbai like the Sea Link. Seasonal additions like the mango chilli margarita bring in a refreshing twist.

When it comes to desserts, this is where you should absolutely give in. The gooey brownie with vanilla ice cream paired with an irresistible mango cream is easily one of the highlights and something you cannot go wrong with.

Overall, Cafe Free India in Lower Parel delivers more than just a meal. With its food, drinks, and high energy karaoke nights, it is a place that promises a fun and memorable outing.
